question.:question/problem:
Given that
$C=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{22}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that
$X=\begin{bmatrix}10 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 8 & 5 & 0\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{12}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\begin{bmatrix}10 & 10 & -8 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 8 & 5 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 8 & 5 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

$A=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 3 \\ -9 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 0 & 6\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{33}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 3 \\ -9 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 0 & 6\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 3 \\ -9 & -5 & 1 \\ -4 & -8 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

$A=\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{23}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -5 & 2 \\ 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -5 & 2 \\ -4 & -8 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

$T=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 6 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix}$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{23}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 6 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}6 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

$T=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 7 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -6\end{bmatrix}$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{12}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 7 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -6\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & -2 \\ 6 & 7 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

$T=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 10 & 6 \\ -6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{12}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 10 & 6 \\ -6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & 10 & 6 \\ -6 & -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

$T=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & 2 \\ 8 & 4 & 6 \\ -6 & -6 & 2\end{bmatrix}$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{11}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & 2 \\ 8 & 4 & 6 \\ -6 & -6 & 2\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & 4 & 6 \\ -6 & -6 & 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}.

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{3}.

question.:question/problem:
Given that
$S=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{31}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 9 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that
$S=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{21}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{3}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given that
$S=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{12}=0?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{3}={R}_{1}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3}
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{3}
$$

or simply

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{3}.
$$
